title: Ghana's Debt Reset: Default, a $3bn IMF Deal and a $13bn Eurobond Swap | The Six, Ep. 20
lede: In December 2022, with inflation heading for 54.1%, Ghana stopped paying most of its foreign debt. Since then it has restructured $13 billion of Eurobonds, finished a $3 billion IMF programme and won rating upgrades from Fitch and Moody's this year. Public debt is now 47.5% of GDP, against a 45% target.
keyPoints: Ghana suspended payments on its Eurobonds, commercial loans and most bilateral loans in December 2022; multilateral lenders were still paid (Reuters via Al Jazeera).

The Eurobond exchange, completed in October 2024 with more than 98% participation, cut about $5 billion from $13 billion of bonds and saved $4.3 billion in debt service during the IMF programme (GNA; MyJoyOnline).
On July 27, 2026 the IMF completed the final review of Ghana's $3 billion programme, releasing about $371 million, and upgraded its risk of debt distress to moderate (IMF).
Moody's raised Ghana to B3 from Caa1 on Oct. 9, 2026; Fitch raised it to B from B- in May (Citi Newsroom; African Economy Inc).
The 2027 budget puts public debt at 47.5% of GDP at end-October 2026, up from 44.7% at end-2025, against a 45% target (2027 Budget via GBC and GhanaWeb).
